public_rationale: Microsoft did make the January 2025 statement. But Amazon had already disclosed a multi-billion-dollar AI revenue run rate in April 2024. Under the ordinary reading that quantified dollar bands count as talking about revenue, Microsoft was not unique. The separate assertion about Microsoft's last disclosure remains unestablished.
limitations: The decisive counterexample gives a dollar band rather than an exact total.
The verdict addresses the uniqueness claim; it does not assert that every clause is false.
Run rates are not realized annual revenue.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft is the only hyperscaler that has ever disclosed actual AI revenue, last in January 2025, and none has done so since.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft was the only hyperscaler to ever talk about actual AI revenues, and last did so in January 2025 when it said it had reached a “$13 billion run rate” (so $1.03 billion). It has never done so again.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

our_interpretation: The target is the disclosure record through March 17, 2026, not disclosures made afterward.
Annualized AI revenue counts because the speaker explicitly accepts Microsoft's run-rate disclosure.
A quantified dollar band such as multi-billion dollars counts as talking about AI revenues; it is less precise than an exact figure but is still a revenue disclosure.
Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet/Google and Meta are within the hyperscaler population.
The metric_scope records the annualized revenue measure explicitly accepted by the speaker. Realized quarterly revenue is retained separately as context.
The parenthetical monthly conversion is not used to decide the normalized disclosure claim.
criteria.support_condition: The disclosure record establishes Microsoft's January 2025 statement and contains neither another hyperscaler's qualifying AI revenue disclosure nor a later qualifying Microsoft disclosure by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A primary record shows another hyperscaler disclosed AI-specific dollar revenue or an annual revenue run rate, or Microsoft made another qualifying disclosure after January 2025 and before the post.
